title: Sport Bolsters Squad Ahead of Série B Final Stretch
seoTitle: Sport Bolsters Squad Ahead of Série B Final Stretch
subtitle: New signings expand tactical options for Mariano Soso
excerpt: With 13 signings and nine departures, Sport overhauled its squad for Série B, seeking more technical alternatives and reinforcing the left-back position after the.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Last Friday, Sport closed the 2026 transfer window with 13 new signings and nine departures, strengthening the squad for the final stretch of Série B. The activity gained prominence following the injury to Felipinho, which left the left-back unable to play for the remainder of this season.

New additions expand tactical options

Among the reinforcements, standout names include left-back Raí Lopes, forwards Neto Pessoa and Kervin Andrade, as well as defensive midfielders Willian Oliveira, Murilo Rhilkman, Patrick de Paula, and Fernando Sobral. Pundit Cabral Neto pointed out that although the overall level of the squad remains similar, the number of options has increased, which could prove positive for head coach Mariano Soso.

Raí Lopes arrives to cover for Felipinho's absence

The left-back, who arrived from Moldova's Sheriff, signed a contract through December 31, 2026, and has already completed medical examinations. He enters into competition with Edson Lucas for the starting role, as Felipinho is recovering from left ankle surgery and is not expected to return in 2026.

Key departures of the window

The club released nine players, including goalkeeper Halls, center-back Zé Marcos, right-back Madson, and defensive midfielders Zé Lucas, Yago Felipe, and Pedro Martins. Cabral Neto viewed the loss of Zé Lucas as the negative aspect of the transfer dealings.

First appearances for the new signings

Fernando Sobral and Patrick de Paula have already made their debuts, coming on as substitutes in the 2-0 victory over Ponte Preta. Murilo Rhilkman has not yet been named to a matchday squad, while the remaining newcomers await opportunities in upcoming matches.

Next steps for the Leão

With 41 points, Sport sits in ninth place and will face CRB next Tuesday at 9:00 p.m. at Rei Pelé Stadium. The board continues to monitor the market, particularly seeking a free-agent right-back, as new registrations outside the window are only permitted for unattached players.

With information from ge, Terra.
